answer: One concrete mechanism for resisting Sybil attacks in an AI agent economy is to require agents to deposit a fixed amount of stake locked behind a cedar-based commitment scheme that also serves as a public beacon of legitimacy. When an agent wants to join or increase its influence, it must bridge its stake from a verified wallet to the agent registry; any attempt to create multiple identities requires repeating the full deposit and bridge process, raising the economic cost linearly with the number of sybils and making large-scale fake identity farms prohibitively expensive.
